Q1: The British. A Union Jack flies over the fortress tower on the Rock in frames 40-41 (Jan 1780), and the town is shown under siege from the land side and the sea throughout.
Q2: The Great Siege. Frame 23 shows the on-screen caption '1779 — The Great Siege'. After that, camp grids spread across the plain, a line of troops and wagons appears, and ships gather in the bay.
Q3: The town is cut off by land and sea. Siege camps and trenches block the landward side, and enemy ships blockade the bay, so food and supplies can't get in. The pictures never show hungry people directly. This is inferred from the blockade and the Jan 1780 scene of people lying on the hillside, and I am not sure of it.
Q4: A fleet of ships, shown arriving in frame 47 (18 Jan 1780), with a supply convoy implied. The pictures don't show clearly that it brings food. In frames 48-49 people carry or load barrels or crates near the walls, and this fits a relief of supplies. I am not sure about the ships' purpose.
